title: Run Tasks With a Cooldown

concept.title: In every round of cool + 1 slots, run the tasks with the most work left
body: Each task is a capital letter; one task takes one time unit. Two tasks with the **same letter** must have at least `cool` time units between them (the units in between may run other tasks or stay idle). What is the shortest time to finish everything?

Think in rounds of `cool + 1` time units. In a round a letter can run at most once, so run **different letters**, and choose the ones with the **most tasks left**, because they are the hardest to fit later. A max-heap of the remaining counts gives them. If after the round some tasks remain, the round took the full `cool + 1` units (idle units included); the last round takes only as many units as it has tasks.

There is also a formula: if the most frequent letter appears `m` times and `c` letters have that count, the answer is `max(number of tasks, (m - 1) * (cool + 1) + c)`. The heap simulation shows why it is true, and it works for harder variants too.

statement: Each task is a capital letter and takes one time unit. Two tasks with the same letter must have at least `cool` time units between them. The tasks can be run in any order, and the processor may be idle. Print the smallest total number of time units needed to run all the tasks.
inputFormat: The first line has the string `tasks`: capital letters, one for each task.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of time units.
constraints: Every task is a capital letter from A to Z.

examples.note: A B idle A B idle A B: 8 time units.

hints: Count how many tasks there are of each letter.
Work in rounds of cool + 1 units and run the letters with the largest counts left.
A round is full length if tasks remain afterwards; the last round lasts as long as the tasks in it.

explanation: Rounds of cool + 1 units run the letters with the most tasks left, taken from a max-heap. A round that leaves tasks behind lasts cool + 1 units, the last round only as long as it has tasks.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

tasks = input().strip()
cool = int(input())

import heapq
counts = {}
for c in tasks:
    counts[c] = counts.get(c, 0) + 1
heap = [-v for v in counts.values()]
heapq.heapify(heap)
time = 0
while heap:
    kept = []
    used = 0
    for _ in range(cool + 1):
        if not heap:
            break
        c = heapq.heappop(heap)
        used += 1
        if c < -1:
            kept.append(c + 1)
    for c in kept:
        heapq.heappush(heap, c)
    time += cool + 1 if heap else used
print(time)
